## Deferred documentation recommendations

- F50. Identify lifecycle, link-integrity, and tracker-maintenance force bypasses as human-operator actions while preserving every supported force surface and distinguishing review-plan recomputation.
- F51. Correct README publication claims so they describe the local-commit guarantee, configured push policy, strict delivery, and observable pending backlog.
- F52A. Remove maintained claims that .rebar/config.conf remains supported while preserving tombstone, migration, test, release-note, and historical references.
- F52B. Correct current operation-certificate descriptions that still call DSSE and SSHSIG verification an HMAC check while preserving generic and legacy HMAC uses.
- F53. Separate external Jira client setup from repository operations, monitoring, fixture maintenance, and Data Center harness procedures.
- F54A. Separate generic MCP client use from repository AWS deployment, SSM, PAT provisioning, rotation, and enforcement operations.
- F54B. Rewrite canonical MCP tool descriptions and generated reference prose in user-facing terms without changing schemas, behavior, generation ownership, or drift enforcement.
- F56. Refactor README by audience while preserving the product overview, plan-review value, tested quickstart, installation, interfaces, client navigation, and MCP ownership marker.
- F57. Label archive, remediation-plan, and experiment material in place rather than moving evidence files.
- F58. Record the implemented plan-review batch boundary and its invariants in a retrospective ADR, then mark the draft design note as implemented historical context.
- F59. Remove activation proof and volatile measurements from the two-vote rollback runbook while preserving operational procedures.
- F55. Keep the two-phase removal of the unused MCP HMAC deployment secret deferred pending infrastructure approval.
- F60. Keep GitHub Issues wording and settings held until the repository setting is reconciled with the operator decision that Issues is disabled and future integration is planned.

## Disposition

These entries are research suggestions only. No implementation is authorized in this session. F02, F03, and F04 remain rejected. F05 and F24 remain deferred. F51 precedes F56 because both edit README.md. F50 precedes F54B where help sources overlap.
